title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is a typed Bourbaki draft headed 'SYSTÈMES de RACINES (2), Tribu n° 59'. It is a preliminary version of the introductory examples in Bourbaki's Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Ch. VI (root systems). It sits inside Grothendieck's 1965 motivic Galois folder, between manuscript pages on 'points motiviques' with values in Z_l, R, W(k), etc. The sheet was presumably used as scrap or mis-filed; its content is unrelated to those notes.

Example I (complex case), in modern terms:
- Let g be a complex semisimple Lie algebra and h a Cartan subalgebra.
- The roots R are the nonzero α in h* with g_α ≠ 0. Their rational span V satisfies V⊗C = h*, and R is a reduced root system in V.
- Every reduced root system comes from a complex semisimple Lie algebra, unique up to isomorphism.
- Automorphisms of g stabilizing h induce all of Aut(R). Inner automorphisms induce exactly the Weyl group W(R).
- Identify V* with a Q-form h^0 of h, and let G be a connected complex Lie group with Lie algebra g. The kernel Γ of exp restricted to h is a lattice in i·h^0 with 2πi·Q(R^∨) ⊆ Γ ⊆ 2πi·P(R^∨).
- Γ equals 2πi·Q(R^∨) if G is simply connected, and 2πi·P(R^∨) if G ≅ Ad g.
- 2πi·P(R^∨)/Γ is the centre Z(G), and Γ/2πi·Q(R^∨) is π_1(G).
- The lattice in V dual to (2πi)^{-1}Γ is generated by the weights of representations of G, i.e. the character lattice X*(T).

Example II (real case) begins: a real semisimple g, maximal compact k, p = k^⊥ for the Killing form, a ⊂ p maximal abelian. This leads to restricted roots, possibly non-reduced, which motivates the non-reduced systems of type BC_n. The page breaks off here.

All of this is standard Cartan–Weyl theory as packaged by Bourbaki (published 1968).
errors: The typescript writes [h,x] = α(x); it should read [h,x] = α(h)x. This is a typo in the original, not a mathematical error.
'Le réseau de V associé à (2πi)^{-1}Γ' should be understood as the lattice dual to (2πi)^{-1}Γ under the pairing between V and h^0. With that reading the statement is correct.

ideas.what: Roots of a complex semisimple Lie algebra relative to a Cartan subalgebra form a reduced root system; classification and existence/uniqueness
ideas.modern_name: Cartan–Weyl theory; Chevalley–Serre existence and uniqueness theorem
ideas.usually_credited_to: Killing, Cartan, Weyl; Chevalley and Serre (1948–1966); Bourbaki exposition (1968)
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Groupes et algèbres de Lie, Ch. VI–VIII

ideas.what: Automorphisms stabilizing h induce Aut(R); inner ones induce W(R)
ideas.modern_name: Aut(g,h) → Aut(R) surjective, with image of inner automorphisms equal to the Weyl group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cartan, Weyl, Chevalley; Bourbaki Ch. VIII

ideas.what: Kernel of exp on the Cartan subalgebra lies between the coroot and coweight lattices; centre and π_1 computed as quotients
ideas.modern_name: Cocharacter lattice of the maximal torus, with Q^∨ ⊆ X_*(T) ⊆ P^∨, Z(G) = P^∨/X_*, π_1 = X_*/Q^∨
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weyl, Cartan; Bourbaki Lie Ch. IX
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki Lie Ch. IX. Analogous root-datum formalism for reductive group schemes appears in SGA 3 (Demazure–Grothendieck).

ideas.what: Restricted roots of a real semisimple Lie algebra via the Cartan decomposition (begins only)
ideas.modern_name: Restricted root system of (g,a), possibly non-reduced (BC_n)
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki Lie Ch. VI examples; Helgason

deep.surprise_reason: This is a Bourbaki internal draft (Tribu n° 59) of the standard root-system examples, all of it now in Bourbaki's published Lie chapters. It has no visible connection to the surrounding motivic notes beyond physical placement in the folder.
transcription_corrections: The image reads '[h,x] = α(x)' (a typo in the original); mathematically it should be α(h)x.
'd'algèbres de Lie g' in the image is presumably intended as 'd'algèbre de Lie g'.
'(resp. 2πiP(R*))' is typed with the dot omitted in the image ('2πi̊P' overstrike); it is the same as 2πi.P(R*).
Handwritten pencil page number '209' at the bottom left is not transcribed.
